items.title: Section: The Fourth Locus Opens — Purifying the Obstructions

items.zh: 云何淨障？謂即如是正修加行諸瑜伽師，由四因緣，能令其心淨除諸障。何等為四？一、遍知自性故；二、遍知因緣故；三、遍知過患故；四、修習對治故。
items.en: What is purifying the obstructions? That is, a yoga practitioner correctly cultivating this preparatory practice is able to purify the mind of its obstructions through four causes and conditions. What are the four? First, thoroughly knowing their own-nature. Second, thoroughly knowing their causes and conditions. Third, thoroughly knowing their dangers. Fourth, cultivating their antidotes.

items.title: The Four Obstructions' Own-Nature: Timidity, Being Covered Over, Discursive Thought, Self-Conceit

items.zh: 云何遍知諸障自性？謂能遍知障有四種。一、怯弱障，二、蓋覆障，三、尋思障，四、自舉障。怯弱障者，謂於出離及於遠離勤修行時，所有染污思慕、不樂、希望、憂惱。蓋覆障者，謂貪欲等五蓋。尋思障者，謂欲尋思等染污尋思。自舉障者，謂於少分下劣智見安隱住中，而自高舉。謂我能得，餘則不爾。
items.en: What is thoroughly knowing the obstructions' own-nature? That is, being able to thoroughly know that there are four kinds of obstruction: first, the obstruction of timidity; second, the obstruction of being covered over; third, the obstruction of discursive thought; fourth, the obstruction of self-conceit. The obstruction of timidity is the defiled longing, discontent, craving, and distress that arise while diligently cultivating renunciation and seclusion. The obstruction of being covered over is the five hindrances, beginning with craving. The obstruction of discursive thought is defiled discursive thought, beginning with the thought of desire. The obstruction of self-conceit is, while abiding at ease in some slight, inferior degree of understanding, becoming self-important, thinking: "I alone am capable of this — others are not."

items.zh: 乃至廣說，如前應知。是名遍知諸障自性。云何遍知諸障因緣？

items.title: Section: The Six Causes of Timidity

items.zh: 謂能遍知初怯弱障，有六因緣。一、由先業增上力故，或由疾病所擾惱故，其身羸劣；二、太過加行；三、不修加行；四、初修加行；五、煩惱熾盛；六、於遠離猶未串習。
items.en: Thoroughly knowing the first, the obstruction of timidity, there are six causes and conditions: first, through the empowering force of past karma, or through affliction by illness, the body becomes weak and frail; second, excessive exertion; third, failing to practise at all; fourth, being a genuine beginner; fifth, the afflictions burning intensely; sixth, not yet being habituated to seclusion.

items.title: Section: The Causes of the Remaining Three Obstructions — Unwise Attention to Each of the Five Hindrances

items.zh: 遍知蓋覆、尋思、自舉障因緣者，謂於隨順蓋覆、尋思及自舉障處所法中，非理作意多分串習，是名蓋覆、尋思、自舉障之因緣。若不作意思惟不淨，而於淨相作意思惟，是名此中非理作意。若不作意思惟慈愍，而於瞋相作意思惟，是名此中非理作意。若不作意思惟明相，而於闇相作意思惟，是名此中非理作意。若不作意思惟奢摩他相，而於親屬、國土、不死，昔所曾更歡娛、戲笑、承奉等事諸惡尋思作意思惟，是名此中非理作意。若不作意思惟緣性緣起，而於三世諸行計我、我所，不如理想作意思惟，是名此中非理作意。
items.en: As for thoroughly knowing the causes of being covered over, discursive thought, and self-conceit: it is habitually engaging, in large part, in unwise attention within matters conducive to being covered over, to discursive thought, and to self-conceit — this is called the cause of being covered over, discursive thought, and self-conceit. Not directing attention to impurity, but instead directing attention to attractive appearance — this is the unwise attention meant here. Not directing attention to loving-kindness, but instead directing attention to a hateful aspect … Not directing attention to the mark of brightness, but instead directing attention to a dark aspect … Not directing attention to the mark of calm-abiding, but instead directing attention, with various unwholesome discursive thoughts, to relatives, homeland, denial of death's nearness … Not directing attention to conditioned dependent origination, but instead conceiving, in an unwise manner, a self and what belongs to a self within the conditioned formations of the three times — this is the unwise attention meant here.

items.title: Section: The Dangers of the Four Obstructions — Failing to Attain, and Falling to the Lower Realms

items.zh: 云何遍知諸障過患？謂遍了知此障有故，於其四種未證不證，已證退失。敗壞瑜伽所有加行，有染污住、有苦惱住，自毀、毀他，身壞命終生諸惡趣。是名遍知諸障過患。
items.en: What is thoroughly knowing the dangers of the obstructions? That is, thoroughly knowing that, because these obstructions exist, one fails to attain the four dhyānas, or, having attained them, loses them again. Yogic practice and its entire preparatory effort are ruined; one abides in a defiled state, abides in a state of distress, harms oneself and harms others, and, upon the body's destruction and life's end, is born into the lower realms. This is called thoroughly knowing the dangers of the obstructions.

items.title: Section: Antidotes — the Six Recollections for Timidity, and Their Specific Applications

items.zh: 謂諸怯弱，總用隨念以為對治。由隨念作意慶悅其心，令諸怯弱已生除遣，未生不生。其身羸劣、太過加行、初修加行，用於精進平等通達以為對治。不修加行，用恭敬聽聞、勤加請問以為對治。煩惱熾盛，用不淨等所緣加行以為對治。若未串習，即用如是思擇方便以為對治。謂我昔於遠離不串習故，今於修習遠離生起怯弱；我若於今不習遠離，於當來世定復如是。故我今者應正思擇，於其遠離捨不喜樂，修習喜樂。
items.en: As for timidity in general, the six recollections serve, altogether, as its antidote: through the mental engagement of recollection, one delights and gladdens the mind, causing timidity already arisen to be dispelled and timidity not yet arisen not to arise. Bodily frailty, excessive exertion, and being a genuine beginner are countered through even diligence and diligence that penetrates all the marks. Failing to practise at all is countered through reverent listening and diligently asking questions. Intensely burning affliction is countered through the fitting purifying-conduct object. Not yet being habituated is countered through this very deliberation … one should rightly discern, and set aside discontent with seclusion, cultivating delight in it instead.

items.zh: 餘蓋覆等非理作意，用彼相違如理作意以為對治。應知是名修習對治。
items.en: The unwise attention behind being covered over, discursive thought, and self-conceit is countered through wise attention, its exact reverse. This should be known as cultivating the antidote.

items.title: Section: The Five Loci Recapped — Locus Four Closes

items.zh: 又遍了知諸障自性，是能障礙、是能染污、是黑品攝、是應遠離。能遍了知如是諸障遠離因緣，方可遠離，故應尋求諸障因緣。能遍了知於應遠離不遠離者有何過患，故應尋求諸障過患。既遠離已，更復尋思：如是諸障，云何來世當得不生？故應尋求修習對治。由是因緣，能令其心淨除諸障。
items.en: Further, thoroughly knowing the obstructions' own-nature — that they obstruct, that they defile, that they belong to the dark category, and that they are to be abandoned … through these causes and conditions, the mind is able to be purified of the obstructions.

items.zh: 當知此中，由隨順教有眾多故，毘鉢舍那亦有眾多；毘鉢舍那有眾多故，令奢摩他亦有眾多。又復即此毘鉢舍那，由所知境無邊際故，當知其量亦無邊際。謂由三門及六種事，一一無邊品類差別，

blocks.text: The fourth locus: purifying the mind of its obstructions, by knowing their nature, causes, dangers, and antidotes.
"Thoroughly knowing their own nature, their causes, their dangers, and their antidotes."

**Timidity**: "defiled longing, discontent, craving, and distress" that arise from feeling far from the goal. **Being covered over**: the hindrances. **Discursive thought**: thoughts of desire, ill will, and the rest. **Self-conceit**: "abiding at ease in some slight, inferior degree of understanding", and thinking oneself superior.

Weakness of body from past karma or illness; excessive exertion; failing to practise at all (Master Cháng Bǎi: not delighting in calm and insight, feeling it is too hard); being a genuine beginner; afflictions burning intensely; and not yet being habituated to seclusion.
Being covered, discursive thought, and conceit all arise from "unwise attention" to matters conducive to them.

"One fails to attain the four absorptions, or having attained them, loses them." Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption is conditioned; it can be lost. "One abides in a defiled state, harms oneself and others."

For timidity, the six recollections (Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, precepts, generosity, gods), which gladden the mind. Bodily frailty, overexertion, and inexperience are countered by balanced effort. For the other three: wise attention, "its exact reverse".

quiz.q: "Yoga practitioners … purify the mind of obstructions" — the English renders 瑜伽師 as "a teacher." How do the lectures describe purifying?
options: both: purifying one's own mind — the practitioner himself; "teacher" is misleading
quiz.why: "A teacher of yogic practice correctly cultivating this preparatory practice is able to purify the mind of its obstructions through four causes." Venerable Miào Jìng: purifying obstructions means clearing the obstructions in one's own mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: there are many obstructions in the mind, and they must be purified for success. Here 瑜伽師 means the practitioner, so "teacher" misleads.

quiz.q: Timidity arises "while cultivating renunciation and seclusion." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two?
options: renunciation is leaving saṃsāra's bonds; seclusion is leaving noise
quiz.why: "The obstruction of timidity is the defiled longing, discontent, craving, and distress that arise while diligently cultivating renunciation and seclusion." Venerable Miào Jìng: renunciation means leaving the bonds of birth and death; seclusion means leaving noise and bustle.

quiz.q: Self-conceit arises "abiding in some slight, inferior understanding." What does Master Cháng Bǎi, citing Miào Jìng, say this is?
options: access concentration — one's slight, inferior calm and insight
quiz.why: "The obstruction of self-conceit is, while abiding at ease in some slight, inferior degree of understanding, becoming self-important, thinking: 'I alone am capable of this — others are not.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: Venerable Miào Jìng explains inferior understanding as access concentration — the slight, inferior calm and insight one has achieved.

quiz.q: Timidity has six causes. How does Venerable Miào Jìng define timidity?
options: lacking confidence, thinking oneself incapable of the noble path
quiz.why: "Thoroughly knowing the first, the obstruction of timidity, there are six causes and conditions." Venerable Miào Jìng: timidity is having no confidence in oneself — thinking oneself incapable of training in the noble path.

quiz.q: What kind of person has the third cause, "failing to practise," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: not fond of calm and insight, content with reading scriptures and bowing
quiz.why: "Third, failing to practise at all." Master Cháng Bǎi: not delighting in calm and insight, feeling it's enough just to read sūtras and bow to the Buddha — such a person is timid towards calm and insight.

quiz.q: Why can attained absorption be lost, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: absorption is conditioned — lose its conditions or fall under obstructing ones and it fades
quiz.why: "Having attained them, loses them again." Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption is a conditioned thing; if one fails to maintain the conditions for its accomplishment, or is controlled by obstructing conditions, it will be lost.

quiz.q: "Timidity in general is countered by recollection" — the English says "the six recollections." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng says only "recollection"; Cháng Bǎi lists the six; the text has just "recollection"
quiz.why: "As for timidity in general, the six recollections serve, altogether, as its antidote." Venerable Miào Jìng: in sum, use the method of recollection to counter timidity. Master Cháng Bǎi: reflecting on the merits of the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, giving, precepts, and heavens. The English "six" is an interpretive addition along Cháng Bǎi's lines.
